newsitem.title: PERU: Gunfire heard at Peru siege site.
newsitem.headline: Gunfire heard at Peru siege site.

text.p: Three bursts of gunfire were heard on Monday at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima where Marxist rebels held 74 hostages.
Witnesses said the bursts were heard in rapid succession from inside the residence around 11:20 a.m. (1620 GMT).
The gunfire was heard after Red Cross mediator Michel Minnig left the residence.
Some police outside the residence went on alert, but others remained calm.
Witnesses said a blue and white helicopter briefly appeared overhead around the time of the shots. There were no immediate reports of injuries.

Gunshots heard previously at the residence during the 27-day-old siege have been attributed to a desire on the part of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels holding the hostages to make their presence felt.
